messages.subject: Boxplot and representation of n
parts:
Hi,

This is a follow up to an R-help question I had asked a while ago
(http://tinyurl.com/2wmzem6). I am plotting a panel of boxplox along
the lines of this example from the documentation:

qplot(factor(cyl), mpg, data = mtcars, geom = "boxplot")

However, I would like to add the information how many members (n) each
of the plotted groups has.

table(as.environment ("package:datasets")$"mtcars"[["cyl"]])

... gives those numbers and with "plain" R graphics one can do

boxplot(lapply(split(mtcars,mtcars[["cyl"]]),function(x)
{return(x[["mpg"]])}),varwidth=T)

Hadley stated in the thread linked to above that "varwidth" isn't
working in ggplot2 - so what might be another option to prettily
include that information?

Thanks, Joh

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: Boxplot and representation of n
parts:
Hi Joh,

This is only a workaround for your suggestion,

mtcars <- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), "transform", n = length(mpg))
qplot(factor(cyl), mpg, data = mtcars, fill = n, geom = "boxplot") +
scale_fill_gradient()

hope this helps,
fernando
